dimension_justifications.soundness: The paper clearly separates the true-law oracle identity from the FIT-frozen fitted-score/CAL statement and consistently labels TEST as descriptive. The supplied claim-evidence map gives concrete support paths, although the result remains conditional on the narrow replay model.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The title, abstract, Figure 1, theorem sequence, Table 1, limitations, conclusion, and mandatory statements form an unusually consistent account of the scope. The 9-page main text is visually clean and the two examined figures are legible. A couple of standalone table and dense-results-navigation choices still make cross-carrier evidence slower to audit than necessary.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The exact oracle-versus-fitted distinction plus legitimate FIT/CAL screening is a clear, useful contribution for the stated count-exchangeable replay endpoint. Its empirical and operational implications are deliberately narrow, so it is a fair rather than broad contribution at present.

paper_summary: This paper studies adaptive stopping for binary pass-count replay, where a uniformly random prefix of a fixed-N task is compared with its full-N binary pass-count decision. It proves an oracle conditional replay-flip identity under the true count mixture, implements a distinct FIT-frozen plug-in score, and uses a Bonferroni empirical-Bernstein CAL screen for a marginal replay guarantee. The reported TEST quantities are explicitly descriptive replay readouts, while ordered deployment, answer correctness, and operational savings are excluded.
strongest_verified_contribution: The manuscript presents a readily auditable claim boundary: c_Hstar is an oracle conditional probability only under the true count law, whereas the implemented BAYES-H score is a different FIT-frozen rule whose operative claim is the CAL-screened marginal replay bound (C01-C03, C12).
strengths: The abstract states the model, oracle/fitted split, FIT/CAL/TEST roles, headline readout, and non-endpoints without conflating them (PDF p. 1).

Figure 1 is an effective standalone orientation device: it visually separates random replay from chronology, true-law oracle theory from the fitted score, and CAL screening from descriptive TEST reporting (PDF p. 2; C12).

Table 1 is compact and independently interpretable: it defines the endpoint, warns that TEST is descriptive, reports the reference and heuristic status, and makes the central comparison scannable (PDF p. 6).

The recurrent scope language is consistent rather than evasive: theory, experiments, drift stress, limitations, conclusion, and Figure 2 all preserve the replay-versus-online and CAL-versus-TEST distinctions (PDF pp. 4-9, 15).

Visual inspection found no clipping, overlap, broken glyphs, or illegible primary labels. Figure 2 uses adequate line styles and direct threshold annotation, and Table 5 remains readable at final PDF size (PDF pp. 15-16).
The PDF is anonymous, has 9 main-text pages before references, and contains both a reproducibility statement and an AI-use statement (PDF pp. 1, 9).
questions: Can the authors label Table 5's replay-flip, mean-k, and count-reduction columns explicitly as descriptive TEST quantities and mark the OMR alpha=.01 row as CAL-only, so the table remains unambiguous when read apart from the preceding appendix prose?

Within the nine-page limit, can the three dense cross-carrier paragraphs in Section 6 be given a short in-main navigation aid (for example, a one-line carrier-to-endpoint/scope map or an earlier explicit pointer to Table 5) without adding new claims?

issues.location: PDF p. 16, Table 5 and caption; especially the OMR alpha=.01 BAYES-H row.
issues.observed_evidence: Table 5 labels one column 'CAL EB UCB' but labels the next three only 'replay flip', 'mean k', and 'count reduction'. Its caption says TEST is a descriptive readout, while the preceding prose (PDF p. 15) is needed to learn that the alpha=.01 OMR row is CAL-side only; the table itself uses dashes but does not name that status.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader who encounters the matrix independently can mistake the unqualified replay columns for a homogeneous evaluation split, or overlook the exceptional CAL-only row. This does not alter the underlying claim but weakens the otherwise exemplary CAL-versus-TEST interface.
issues.required_fix: Rename the three outcome columns to 'descriptive TEST replay flip', 'TEST mean k', and 'TEST count reduction' (or an equally compact equivalent), and add a 'CAL only' marker or footnote to the alpha=.01 row.
issues.verification_test: Read Table 5, caption, and footnote without Appendix F prose: every numeric column and every row's evaluation status should be identifiable, including the alpha=.01 exception.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment; a typography/table-label revision using existing supplied values.

issues.location: PDF pp. 6-7, Section 6 'Experiments', notably the second-shard, OpenR1, and RLVE paragraphs.
issues.observed_evidence: The main result is well exposed in Table 1, but the three further carrier settings, their split/accounting distinctions, quantitative readouts, and scope caveats are delivered in long prose blocks. The reader must retain several N/M, split, and endpoint distinctions before reaching the detailed consolidation in appendix Table 5.
issues.why_it_matters: The prose is accurate and its caveats are valuable, but its density makes the evidence topology harder to recover on a first read. This is a navigation cost, not a reason to treat the deliberately narrow contribution as a writing failure.
issues.required_fix: Add a minimal in-main navigation aid or sharper early pointer to Table 5 that names each carrier, its N/M setting, and the descriptive-only status; preserve the existing boundary language rather than expanding claims.
issues.verification_test: A reader should be able to identify, from Section 6 plus its immediate table/pointer, which carrier supports each reported replay readout and that none supports ordered-online, correctness, or operational-cost claims.
issues.evidence_needed: No new evidence; a space-neutral organization or cross-reference revision.

ethics_concerns: No direct ethics violation is apparent in the frozen submission. The paper appropriately states that replay savings do not measure delivered-answer correctness, tokens, latency, cancellation, or an ordered online deployment outcome (PDF pp. 1, 8-9).
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. The manuscript itself includes an AI-use statement (PDF p. 9).
evidence_that_would_raise_score: New evidence directly testing an ordered online stopping policy against the stated replay assumptions and reporting stopped-answer correctness plus operational token/latency/cancellation outcomes could expand the contribution beyond the current replay-only ceiling.
An independently reproducible broader-carrier evaluation with the same predeclared FIT/CAL/TEST protocol could strengthen the current setting-specific empirical contribution.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Evidence that FIT/CAL independence, the frozen candidate family, or the claimed TEST-descriptive status was not maintained would undermine the central exposition and guarantee boundary.
A contradiction between the displayed oracle/fitted/CAL/TEST distinctions and the supplied artifacts would reduce confidence materially.
review_limitations: This is a clarity/presentation review of the frozen snapshot, not an independent rerun or full technical proof verification.
The review does not claim an exhaustive external-literature assessment beyond the supplied snapshot.
